abstract_en: We conducted a component network meta-analysis (CNMA) of phase 3/4 randomized trials to evaluate incremental effects of pharmacological therapies in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF; LVEF > 40%). MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane were searched through 1 August 2025 (updated 30 March 2026). We performed an additive CNMA evaluating cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) and assessed certainty of evidence. Twenty-four trials and five secondary reports were included. The primary network was sparse (10 trials, 12 regimens), constraining interaction detection and component stability. Incretin-based interventions (pooling semaglutide and tirzepatide, iHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.53-0.91), SGLT-2 inhibitors (0.80, 0.74-0.88), ARNis (0.82, 0.68-0.99), and MRAs (0.89, 0.81-0.98) showed significant component associations, driven principally by fewer HFHs. No drug class significantly reduced mortality. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs remained significant across sensitivity analyses except LVEF ≥ 50%, with SGLT-2 inhibitors most precise. ARNi benefits lost significance under stricter background therapy thresholds (>60%) and contemporary trial restrictions. Evidence for incretins was low-certainty and sensitive to trial selection. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs provide the most robust incremental benefit, while evidence for other drug classes remains context-dependent. These findings should guide research priorities rather than define combination regimens. http://www.crd.york.ac.uk PROSPEROidentifier is CRD420251107058.

Se realizó un metaanálisis de red de componentes (CNMA) de ensayos aleatorizados de fase 3/4 para evaluar los efectos incrementales de las terapias farmacológicas en insuficiencia cardiaca con fracción de eyección levemente reducida o conservada (HFmrEF/HFpEF; FEVI > 40%). MEDLINE, Embase y Cochrane fueron buscados hasta el 1o de agosto de 2025 (actualizado el 30 de marzo de 2026). Se realizó un CNMA aditivo evaluando la muerte cardiovascular o la primera hospitalización por insuficiencia cardiaca (HFH) y se evaluó la certeza de la evidencia. Se incluyeron 24 ensayos y cinco informes secundarios. La red primaria fue escasa (10 ensayos, 12 regímenes), limitando la detección de interacciones y estabilidad de componentes. Las intervenciones basadas en la incretina (combinación de semaglutida y tirzepatida, iHR 0,69, IC 95% 0,53-0,91), inhibidores SGLT-2 (0,80, 0,74-0,88), ARNis (0,82, 0,68-0,99) y ARM (0,89, 0,81-0,98) mostraron asociaciones significativas de componentes, impulsadas principalmente por menos HHF. Ninguna clase de fármacos redujo significativamente la mortalidad. Los inhibidores SGLT-2 y ARM permanecieron significativos en los análisis de sensibilidad excepto FEVI ≥ 50%, con inhibidores SGLT-2 más precisos. Los inhibidores de SGLT-2 y los ARM proporcionan el beneficio incremental más sólido, mientras que la evidencia para otras clases de fármacos sigue dependiendo del contexto.Estos hallazgos deben guiar las prioridades de investigación en lugar de definir regímenes de combinación. http://www.crd.york.ac.uk PROSPEROidentifier is CRD420251107058.

abstract_en: Direct-acting oral anticoagulation did not reduce recurrent stroke compared with aspirin in randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), and subgroup benefits suggested by analyses of individual RCTs were inconsistent across trials. We aimed to evaluate the effect of anticoagulation on the risks of recurrent stroke and major bleeding in patients with ESUS, overall and in prespecified subgroups using individual participant data from RCTs. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE and Scopus for RCTs published between April 1, 2014, and March 1, 2025, without language restriction, comparing anticoagulants with aspirin in patients with ESUS. Non-randomised studies and studies not enrolling patients with ESUS were excluded. We requested individual participant data from the principal investigators of all eligible trials. The primary outcomes were recurrent stroke and major bleeding. For each outcome of interest, we estimated the treatment effect for the overall trial population separately within each trial and the resulting overall treatment estimates were subsequently pooled across trials. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version 2.0) for the primary efficacy outcome of stroke recurrence. Hazard ratios (HRs) with corresponding 95% CIs were estimated following adjustment for prespecified covariates and pooled by use of the random-effects model. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025644724). Our systematic database search identified 1170 records. Of these studies, four were eligible for inclusion in the analysis, including a total of 13 970 participants. Mean age of participants was 66 years (SD 10·6); 5486 (39·3%) participants were female and 8484 (60·7%) were male. Across all trials, 6989 patients were assigned to receive a direct-acting oral anticoagulant and 6981 were assigned to receive aspirin. The hazard for recurrent stroke was similar between participants allocated to anticoagulant or aspirin (399 of 6989 patients [4·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 417 of 6981 [4·8 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·78-1·14), without evidence of heterogeneity across studies (I2=5%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·37). The hazard for major bleeding was also similar between the two groups (149 of 6989 patients [1·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 106 of 6981 [1·1 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 1·19, 95% CI 0·52-2·73), but heterogeneity was present across studies (I2=79%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·0023). Anticoagulation did not reduce the risk of recurrent stroke after ESUS when compared with aspirin, and the risk of major bleeding did not differ significantly between the two treatments. A possible benefit from anticoagulation in patients with ESUS and left atrial enlargement, as shown in a hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis, should be investigated in future trials. La anticoagulación oral de acción directa no redujo el accidente cerebrovascular recurrente en comparación con la aspirina en ensayos controlados aleatorizados (TRC) de accidente cerebrovascular embólico de origen indeterminado (ESUS), y los beneficios de subgrupos sugeridos por los análisis de ECA individuales fueron inconsistentes en todos los ensayos. En esta revisión y metaanálisis sistemáticos, se buscó MEDLINE y Scopus para los ECA publicados entre el 1 de abril de 2014 y el 1 de marzo de 2025, sin restricción del lenguaje, comparando anticoagulantes con aspirina en pacientes con ESUS. Se excluyeron estudios no aleatorizados y estudios que no inscribieran a pacientes con ESUS. Se solicitaron datos de participantes individuales de los principales investigadores de todos los ensayos elegibles. Los resultados principales fueron ictus recurrente y hemorragia mayor. Para cada resultado de interés, se estimó el efecto del tratamiento para la población total del ensayo por separado dentro de cada ensayo y las estimaciones resultantes del tratamiento global fueron agrupadas posteriormente en todos los ensayos. Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo con la herramienta Cochrane Risk of Bias (versión 2.0) para el resultado primario de eficacia de la recurrencia del accidente cerebrovascular, se estimaron los coeficientes de riesgo (HR) con IC del 95% correspondientes tras el ajuste por covariables preespecificados y agrupados por el uso del modelo de efectos aleatorios, este estudio se registró con PROSPERO (CRD42025644724), en cuya búsqueda sistemática se identificaron 1170 registros, de los cuales cuatro fueron elegibles para ser incluidos en el análisis, incluyendo un total de 13 970 participantes.La edad media de los participantes fue de 66 años (SD 10·6); 5486 (39·3%) participantes fueron mujeres y 8484 (60·7%) varones. En todos los ensayos, se asignó a 6989 pacientes para recibir un anticoagulante oral de acción directa y 6981 para recibir aspirina.El riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular recurrente fue similar entre los participantes asignados a anticoagulante o aspirina (399 de 6989 pacientes [4,6 eventos por cada 100 pacientes-año] en el grupo anticoagulante frente a 417 de 6981 [4,8 eventos por cada 100 pacientes-año] en el grupo aspirina; FC ajustada 0·94, IC 95% 0·78-1·14), sin evidencia de heterogeneidad en los estudios (I2=5%, p para la prueba Q de Cochran=0·37). El riesgo de hemorragia mayor también fue similar entre los dos grupos (149 de 6989 pacientes [1·6 eventos por cada 100 pacientes-año] en el grupo anticoagulante frente a 106 de 6981 [1·1 eventos por cada 100 pacientes-año] en el grupo de aspirina; FC ajustada 1·19, IC 95% 0·52-2·73), pero la heterogeneidad estuvo presente en los estudios (I2=79%, p para la prueba Q de Cochran=0·0023). La anticoagulación no redujo el riesgo de ictus recurrente después de ESUS en comparación con la aspirina, y el riesgo de hemorragia mayor no difirió significativamente entre los dos tratamientos. Un posible beneficio de la anticoagulación en pacientes con ESUS y ampliación auricular izquierda, como se muestra en un análisis de subgrupos de hipótesis generadoras, debe ser investigado en futuros ensayos.División de Fondo de Innovación Neurológica, Universidad McMaster.

abstract_en: The optimal antithrombotic therapy (ATT) for patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) is still a matter of debate. In this regard, the role of low-dose rivaroxaban remains controversial. The authors performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCT) comparing low-dose rivaroxaban vs standard ATT across the spectrum of CAD. RCTs were searched through MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases, and international meeting proceedings. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Results are reported as incidence rate ratio (IRR) of low-dose rivaroxaban vs standard ATT. Five trials including 37 709 randomized patients were identified. Low-dose rivaroxaban was associated with significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality (IRR = 0.83; 95% CI, 0.70-0.98; P = .02), driven by a significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality (IRR = 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69-0.97; P = .02). Low-dose rivaroxaban was also associated with a significant reduction in myocardial infarction (IRR = 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.99; P = .04), major adverse cardiovascular events (IRR = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.76-0.95; P less than .01), and stroke (IRR = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.55-0.91; P less than .01). Stroke reduction was driven by a significant reduction in ischemic strokes (IRR = 0.60; 95% CI, 0.49-0.74; P less than .01), not offset by an increase in hemorrhagic strokes. In contrast, low-dose rivaroxaban increased major bleeding (IRR = 1.46; 95% CI, 0.99-2.17), but not fatal bleeding. In patients with CAD, low-dose rivaroxaban significantly reduces all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and stroke, but increases major bleeding compared with standard ATT.

La dosis baja de rivaroxaban se asoció con tasas significativamente más bajas de mortalidad por todas las causas (IRR = 0,83; IC 95%, 0,70-0,98; P = 0,02), impulsadas por una reducción significativa de la mortalidad cardiovascular (IRR = 0,82; IC 95%, 0,69-0,97; P = 0,02). La dosis baja de rivaroxaban también se asoció con una reducción significativa del infarto de miocardio (IRR = 0,88; IC 95%, 0,79-0,99; P = 0,04), los eventos cardiovasculares adversos mayores (IRR = 0,85; IC 95%, 0,76-0,95; P menos de 0,01), y el accidente cerebrovascular (IRR = 0,71; IC 95%, 0,55-0,91; P menos de 0,01). En contraste, la dosis baja de rivaroxaban aumentó la hemorragia mayor (IRR = 1,46; IC 95%, 0,99-2,17), pero no la hemorragia mortal.En pacientes con EAC, la dosis baja de rivaroxaban reduce significativamente la mortalidad por todas las causas, la mortalidad cardiovascular y el accidente cerebrovascular, pero aumenta la hemorragia mayor en comparación con la ATT estándar.

title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.

abstract_en: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras. PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized trials directly comparing CAS with CEA in adults with extracranial carotid stenosis. Arm-level event counts were extracted. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using inverse-variance models with DerSimonian-Laird estimation. Hartung-Knapp intervals and absolute risk differences were added to support sensitivity analysis and clinical interpretation. The primary endpoint was 30-day stroke or death. Secondary endpoints included periprocedural stroke, death, myocardial infarction (MI), cranial nerve injury, disabling stroke or death, and exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes. Six randomized cohorts contributed to the primary endpoint; up to eight contributed to secondary analyses. Thirty-day stroke or death occurred in 244 of 5285 patients assigned to CAS (4.6%) and 156 of 4522 assigned to CEA (3.4%), corresponding to an absolute excess of 1.2 percentage points with CAS and a pooled RR of 1.42 (95% CI, 1.12-1.81; I²=27.9%). Periprocedural stroke was also more common after CAS (291/6305 [4.6%] vs. 186/5546 [3.4%]; RR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.18-1.75; I²=9.1%). Periprocedural death did not differ significantly (RR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.77-2.19). MI (RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.29-0.71) and cranial nerve injury (RR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.11) favored CAS. In a prespecified sensitivity analysis excluding CAVATAS-because most patients in its endovascular arm underwent balloon angioplasty rather than stenting-the primary result was unchanged (RR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.17-1.95). Exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes did not differ significantly (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87-1.26), although endpoint definitions and follow-up windows varied substantially. In randomized head-to-head trials, CAS was associated with higher early stroke and stroke-or-death risk than CEA, whereas MI and cranial nerve injury were reported less often after CAS. Selection of open versus endovascular carotid revascularization should be guided by symptom status, age, lesion morphology, cervical and arch anatomy, perioperative cardiac risk, and operator outcomes.

La endarterectomía carotídea (ECA) sigue siendo la estrategia de revascularización abierta de referencia para pacientes adecuadamente seleccionados con estenosis carotídea extracraneal, mientras que el stent endovascular de la arteria carotídea (CAS) proporciona una alternativa endovascular cuando la exposición cervical, la comorbilidad médica o los factores anatómicos hacen que la cirugía abierta sea menos favorable. PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL y ClinicalTrials.gov fueron investigados hasta abril de 2026. Los estudios elegibles fueron ensayos aleatorizados que compararon directamente CAS con CEA en adultos con estenosis carotídea extracraneal; se extrajeron recuentos de eventos a nivel de brazo; se calcularon ratios de riesgo de efectos aleatorios (RRs) con intervalos de confianza (IC) del 95% utilizando modelos de variación inversa con estimación DerSimonian-Laird; se añadieron intervalos de Hartung-Knapp y diferencias de riesgo absolutas para apoyar el análisis de sensibilidad e interpretación clínica; la variable principal fue el ictus o muerte de 30 días. Los criterios de valoración secundarios fueron: ictus periprocedimiento, muerte, infarto de miocardio (IM), lesión del nervio craneal, ictus o muerte incapacitante, y desenlaces exploratorios relacionados con el ictus a largo plazo. Seis cohortes aleatorias contribuyeron a la variable primaria; hasta ocho contribuyeron a análisis secundarios. El ictus o muerte de treinta días se produjo en 244 de los 5285 pacientes asignados a CAS (4,6%) y 156 de los 4522 asignados a ACE (3,4%), lo que corresponde a un exceso absoluto de 1,2 puntos porcentuales con CAS y un RR agrupado de 1,42 (IC 95%, 1,12-1,81; I2=27,9%). El ictus periprocedimiento también fue más frecuente después de CAS (291/6305 [4,6%] vs. 186/5546 [3,4%]; RR, 1,44; IC 95%, 1,18-1,75; I2=9,1%). La muerte periprocedimiento no difirió significativamente (RR, 1,30; IC 95%, 0,77-2,19). MI (RR, 0,45; IC 95%, 0,29-0,71) y lesión del nervio craneal (RR, 0,05; IC 95%, 0,02-0.11) favorecieron el CAS. En un análisis de sensibilidad preespecificado excluyendo el CAVTAS-porque la mayoría de los pacientes en su brazo endovascular se sometieron a angioplastia con balón en lugar de stent-el resultado primario fue sin cambios (RR, 1,51; IC 95%, 1,17-1,95). Los resultados exploratorios a largo plazo relacionados con el ictus no difirieron significativamente (RR, 1,05; IC 95%, 0,87-1,26), aunque las definiciones de la variable y las ventanas de seguimiento variaron sustancialmente. En los ensayos aleatorizados de cabeza a cabeza, el CAS se asoció con mayor riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular y muerte por accidente cerebrovascular que el CEA, mientras que el IM y la lesión del nervio craneal se notificaron con menos frecuencia después del CAS. La selección de revascularización carótida abierta frente a la endovascular debe guiarse por el estado sintomático, la edad, la morfología de la lesión, la anatomía cervical y arqueológica, el riesgo cardíaco perioperatorio y los resultados del operador.

abstract_en: To evaluate associations of metformin exposure with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and lactic or metabolic acidosis in adults with Type 2 diabetes and advanced CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) not receiving chronic dialysis. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane from inception through 5 September 2026 for observational cohort studies evaluating metformin exposure in this population. Comparator strategies included non-use, discontinuation and alternative glucose-lowering therapy. Data were synthesized using Bayesian random-effects models with empirical heterogeneity priors (primary) and frequentist random-effects models. Certainty of the evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework. Ten cohort studies were included. For ESKD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) from the Bayesian analysis was 0.64 (95% CrI: 0.45-0.92; 99% posterior probability of HR < 1). Estimates for MACE (HR 0.88, 95% CrI: 0.72-1.08) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CrI: 0.73-1.10) were imprecise. Lactic or metabolic acidosis showed an increased-risk estimate with a wide CrI (HR 1.39, 95% CrI: 0.76-2.49). Certainty of the evidence was very low for all outcomes. For ESKD, the pooled Bayesian estimate was below the null, whereas estimates for all-cause mortality and MACE remained uncertain, and an increased risk of acidosis could not be excluded. Given the very low certainty of the evidence and the heterogeneity of treatment strategies, these findings should be interpreted with considerable caution. Further randomized or well-designed observational evidence using clearly defined treatment strategies is needed.

Para evaluar las asociaciones de exposición a metformina con mortalidad por cualquier causa, eventos cardiovasculares adversos (MACE), enfermedad renal terminal (ESKD) y acidosis láctica o metabólica en adultos con diabetes tipo 2 y ERC avanzada (tasa de filtración glomerular estimada (eGFR) < 30 mL/min/1,73 m2) que no recibían diálisis crónica. Buscamos PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science y Cochrane desde el inicio hasta el 5 de septiembre de 2026 para estudios observacionales de cohorte que evaluaran la exposición a metformina en esta población. Los datos fueron sintetizados utilizando modelos de efectos aleatorios bayesianos con antecedentes empíricos de heterogeneidad (primaria) y modelos de efectos aleatorios frecuente.La certeza de la evidencia fue evaluada utilizando el marco GRADE.Se incluyeron diez estudios de cohorte.Para ESKD, la razón de riesgo conjunta (HR) del análisis bayesiano fue 0,64 (IC 95%: 0,45-0,92; probabilidad posterior de FC 99% < 1).Las estimaciones para MACE (HR 0,88, IC 95%: 0,72-1,08) y mortalidad por cualquier causa (CRI 0,89, IC 95%: 0,73-1,10) fueron imprecisas.La acidosis láctica o metabólica mostró una estimación de riesgo aumentada con una CrI amplia (CRI 1,39, IC 95%: 0,76-2,49).La certeza de la evidencia fue muy baja para todos los resultados. abstract_en: Abstract  Background  Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is an important cause of maternal cardiovascular mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries due to limited access to specialized cardiac care. This systematic review aims to synthesize evidence on the proportions of mortality, recovery of left ventricular function, cardiovascular complications, and maternal and obstetric characteristics among women with PPCM in Pakistan. Methods  A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Google Scholar, PakMediNet, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 to May 2026 for studies reporting PPCM outcomes in Pakistan and registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420261403054). Eligible studies included observational studies and case series involving women diagnosed with PPCM. Extracted data included study design, sample size, mortality, recovery of left ventricular systolic function, cardiovascular complications, and obstetric characteristics. Pooled proportions were calculated descriptively using aggregate study data. The quality of study was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Results  Seven studies were included. Mortality outcomes were reported in six studies including 315 patients, with 49 deaths recorded, yielding an overall mortality proportion of 15.6%. Recovery of left ventricular systolic function was reported in four studies including 160 patients, of whom 97 achieved recoveries, corresponding to an overall recovery proportion of 60.6%, predominantly defined by improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction during 6–12 months of follow-up. Pulmonary edema was the most frequently reported cardiovascular complication (21.6%), while thromboembolic events (17.9%), cardiogenic shock (13.1%), ventricular tachycardia (9.9%), and atrial fibrillation (9.4%) occurred less frequently. Among the reported maternal characteristics, obesity was the most common (62.9%). Multiparity was the predominant obstetric characteristic (69.1%), whereas pregnancy-related hypertensive disorders, primigravidity, and multiple gestation were reported in 34.1%, 22.9%, and 9.7% of women, respectively. Conclusion  PPCM in Pakistan remains associated with considerable mortality and a substantial burden of cardiovascular complications. Obesity, multiparity, and pregnancy-related hypertensive disorders were the predominant maternal and obstetric characteristics, highlighting the importance of early recognition, timely cardiac assessment, and multidisciplinary care to improve maternal outcomes. abstract_en: Lactate occupies a paradoxical position in critical care. Traditionally regarded as a marker of physiological stress, it is increasingly recognized as an important metabolic substrate with potential therapeutic effects. In their meta-analysis of randomized trials, Labenbacher and colleagues summarize the current clinical evidence for hypertonic sodium lactate treatment (HSL) across heterogeneous critically ill populations. Although no mortality benefit can be established, the available evidence raises several important mechanistic and methodological questions. First, "lactate therapy" is not a single intervention as HSL simultaneously alters lactate availability, sodium load, tonicity, and acid-base balance. Second, currently used regimens differ markedly in dose, duration, and achieved plasma lactate concentrations, precluding a meaningful dose-exposure-response framework. Third, the physiological response may depend strongly on the underlying hemodynamic and metabolic phenotype with signals of improved cardiac output in some cardiovascular settings but inconsistent findings across other disease states. At this stage, the key question is therefore not simply whether lactate "works" nor whether it improves mortality, but which physiological effect is being targeted, in which patient phenotype, at what exposure, and through which mechanism. Future studies should disentangle the metabolic, osmotic, vascular, and acid-base effects of lactate-containing solutions before definitive clinical outcome trials are undertaken.

abstract_en:
Objective
Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become a foundational therapy for adult heart failure across the entire spectrum of ejection fraction, but their safety profile in children with heart failure has not been quantitatively synthesized. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions to summarize the incidence of adverse events associated with SGLT2 inhibitors in pediatric heart failure.Study design
In this systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions (PROSPERO CRD420261355711; PRISMA 2020), five databases were searched through June 2026 for studies of any design reporting adverse events among pediatric patients receiving an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart failure. Random-effects incidence estimates were pooled using logit-transformed proportions with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals; risk of bias and GRADE certainty were assessed.Results
Ten studies (573 unique children; 2023-2026) were included; eight studies (572 patients; maximum pooled denominator 474) were meta-analyzed, and one case report was summarized narratively. Dapagliflozin accounted for 94.1% of exposures. Study-level dapagliflozin doses ranged from 0.11 to 0.23 mg/kg/day, while the single cohort reporting empagliflozin used a median dose of 0.13 mg/kg/day. No regimen was derived from pediatric heart-failure pharmacokinetic data, and in the only cohort reporting a comparison, infants received a higher weight-normalized dose than older children (0.18 versus 0.16 mg/kg/day). Pooled incidences were: any adverse event 21.2% (95% CI 10.7-37.8%), acute kidney injury 10.7% (3.5-28.1%), urinary tract infection 7.8% (4.8-12.4%), treatment discontinuation 7.0% (4.5-10.6%), all-cause mortality 5.6% (2.4-12.5%), hypoglycemia 2.9% (0.9-9.3%), genital mycotic infection 2.7% (0.9-8.2%), and diabetic ketoacidosis 1.3% (0.4-3.9%). No deaths were attributed to therapy, and no cases of euglycemic ketoacidosis or Fournier gangrene occurred. Directional efficacy signals were consistently favorable, with left ventricular ejection fraction improving in five of six cohorts and natriuretic peptide levels declining across all seven in which they were assessed.Conclusions
SGLT2 inhibitors had a tolerable safety profile in pediatric heart failure, mirroring the adult experience. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized adverse-event grading are needed.Registration

abstract_en: Hypertension significantly contributes to the risk of cardiovascular disease and associated mortality. The timing of medication use and associated cardiovascular outcomes is not well established, with conflicting results. We evaluated the association between morning versus evening antihypertensive medication and cardiovascular outcomes. We performed a systematic literature search on PubMed, Scopus, and ClinicalTrial.gov for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from inception until June 5, 2026. Studies were considered eligible for inclusion if patients with hypertension received antihypertensive medication in the intervention group during the morning/daytime and in the control group in the evening. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effect model, and a P value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Six RCTs with 46,857 patients (23,488 assigned to morning antihypertensive medication and 23,369 assigned to evening antihypertensive medication) were included in the analysis. The mean age of patients was 63.3 years. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant difference between morning and evening antihypertensive medication dosing for all-cause mortality (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.92-1.85, P = 0.14), major adverse cardiovascular events (OR 1.28, 95% CI 0.93-1.76, P = 0.13), or stroke (OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.96-2.19, P = 0.08). Use of the HSP technique for vascular access haemostasis after TAVR or pEVAR was associated with significantly lower rates of vascular complications, bleeding, and VCD failure compared with SO closure, without a significant difference in mortality.

abstract_en: BackgroundTotal coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT) is a sternum-sparing approach to multivessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Published evidence is predominantly observational. This review summarizes reported perioperative outcomes after TCRAT; its principal quantitative synthesis is single-arm and does not establish comparative effectiveness against conventional CABG.MethodsThis systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidance and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437661). PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception to May 1, 2026. Studies reporting perioperative or clinical outcomes in adults undergoing TCRAT were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and the JBI checklist for case series. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions used the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation; continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation.ResultsSeven cohorts comprising a reported total of 1869 patients were included. The pooled in-hospital/short-term mortality estimate was 0.92% (95% CI, 0.28-1.83%; I2 = 48.8%), and the pooled stroke estimate was 0.76% (95% CI, 0.10-1.82%; I2 = 61.6%). Pooled incidences of postoperative atrial fibrillation and re-exploration were 11.53% and 3.44%, respectively; deep wound infection was uncommon (0.15%). Pooled mean cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 146.17 and 78.05 minutes. Estimates for operative times and length of stay were highly heterogeneous. The exploratory diabetes-stratified analysis did not detect a statistically significant mortality difference (p = 0.8443).ConclusionThe available cohorts describe the perioperative outcomes reported after TCRAT in selected patients and centers. These single-arm pooled estimates should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence, superiority, or non-inferiority compared with conventional CABG. Larger, well-adjusted comparative studies with standardized outcomes and long-term follow-up are needed.

abstract_en:
Objective
To compare vascular complications between percutaneous and surgical access during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation (tf-TAVI) and estimate pooled outcomes following percutaneous access.Design
Systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative and single-arm studies.Data sources and review methods
PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 8 July 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261454909). Comparative (odds ratio [OR]) and single-arm (pooled proportion) random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Subgroup, meta-regression, sensitivity, and publication-bias analyses were conducted for the primary outcome. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I, ROBINS-I Single Arm, and RoB 2.Results
Ten comparative studies (4 736 patients) and eight single-arm studies (5 113 patients) were included. Major vascular complications did not differ significantly between percutaneous access and surgical cutdown (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.61-1.14; I2 = 41.8%; 95% prediction interval 0.39-1.78), with no significant differences in secondary clinical outcomes, including hospital length of stay (mean difference -0.96 days, 95% CI -2.38 to 0.47; p = .19). In the single-arm analysis, pooled major vascular complications after percutaneous TAVI were 5.20% (95% CI 3.52-7.63%; 95% prediction interval 1.43-17.21%; I2 = 91.1%), with 30-day mortality of 2.20% (95% CI 1.41-3.40%; 95% prediction interval 0.72-6.46%; I2 = 66.9%). Funnel plot asymmetry (Egger's p = .034) was attributable to a single zero-event study and was not confirmed by the Peters test (p = .651) or after its exclusion (p = .164).Conclusion
Percutaneous femoral access was not associated with a statistically significant difference in major vascular complications or other clinically relevant outcomes compared with surgical cutdown in anatomically suitable patients treated at experienced centres; residual confounding cannot be excluded, and this evidence is largely observational and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending confirmation in randomized trials.Registration
PROSPERO (CRD420261454909).

abstract_en:
Background
Severe aortic stenosis and coronary artery disease frequently coexist in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We compared planned percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) around TAVI with an initially conservative or deferred PCI strategy.Methods
We searched PubMed, Cochrane, Scopus, and Web of Science through 15 April 2026. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Exploratory reconstruction was a secondary analysis. The study protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO with the following ID: CRD420261397950.Results
Three randomized controlled trials including 1156 patients were identified. Planned PCI was not associated with significant differences in all-cause mortality (risk ratio = 0.90, 95% CI = 0.70-1.15), trial-defined major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; risk ratio = 0.91, 95% CI = 0.70-1.18; supportive and exploratory because composite components differed), cardiovascular death (risk ratio = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.51-1.08), or myocardial infarction (risk ratio = 0.86, 95% CI = 0.45-1.63). It was associated with fewer urgent (risk ratio = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.13-0.87) and any subsequent revascularizations (risk ratio = 0.25, 95% CI = 0.07-0.87), but more trial-reported major bleeding (risk ratio = 1.57, 95% CI = 1.07-2.32; definitions varied) and any bleeding (risk ratio = 1.77, 95% CI = 1.27-2.47).Conclusion
Routine planned PCI around TAVI was not shown to reduce mortality or major ischemic outcomes. It was associated with fewer subsequent revascularizations and more trial-reported major bleeding and any bleeding, supporting selective, individualized decision-making.

abstract_en:
Background
Ventricular fibrillation (VF) and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PVT) are major causes of sudden cardiac death. Although Purkinje-targeted catheter ablation has emerged as a rescue therapy for refractory ventricular arrhythmias, the comparative safety and efficacy of trigger-focused ablation versus Purkinje de-networking (PDN) remain uncertain.Objective
To synthesize clinical outcomes for Purkinje-targeted interventions across diverse arrhythmic phenotypes.Methods
We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Ovid, and CENTRAL for studies enrolling adults with recurrent or refractory ventricular fibrillation (VF) or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PVT). We performed pairwise and network meta-analyses using random-effects models. We evaluated the certainty of evidence using GRADE frameworks (PROSPERO: CRD420261423684).Results
We included 22 studies involving 959 patients. Among PDN cohorts, pooled mortality was 13.5% (n = 435; 16 cohorts; 95% CI: 9.0%-20.1%; I2 = 99.28%), acute success was 83.5% (n = 388; 14 cohorts; 95% CI: 78.9%-88.4%; I2 = 34.33%), and VF/PVT recurrence was 18.9% (n = 412; 15 cohorts; 95% CI: 15.7%-22.6%; I2 = 0%). Compared with standard ablation, PDN showed nonsignificant reductions in mortality (RR 0.672, 95% CI: 0.267-1.69; I2 = 0%) and recurrence (RR 0.820, 95% CI: 0.239-2.807; I2 = 70.33%). In the primary network meta-analysis, PDN ranked highest for acute success (SUCRA 86.27%) and freedom from recurrence (77.05%). However, in a sensitivity analysis of comparative trials (9 trials; n = 457), trigger-focused ablation ranked highest for acute success (SUCRA 88.08% vs. 51.52% for PDN). New-onset LBBB occurred in up to 20.8% after substrate-based PDN.Conclusions
In this exploratory network meta-analysis, PDN ranked favorably for acute procedural success and short-term arrhythmia freedom. However, low-certainty evidence, imprecise estimates, and substantial clinical heterogeneity preclude definitive conclusions about its comparative efficacy. Large-scale randomized trials are needed to establish its clinical benefit.

Entre las cohortes PDN, la mortalidad agrupada fue del 13,5% (n = 435; 16 cohortes; IC 95%: 9,0%-20,1%; I2 = 99,28%), el éxito agudo fue del 83,5% (n = 388; 14 cohortes; IC 95%: 78,9%-88,4%; I2 = 34,33%), y la recurrencia de FV/PVT fue del 18,9% (n = 412; 15 cohortes; IC 95%: 15,7%-22,6%; I2 = 0%). Se necesitan ensayos aleatorizados a gran escala para establecer su beneficio clínico.

abstract_en:
Background
Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs.Methods
Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies of adults with diabetes in LMICs reporting LLA with adjusted effect estimates were included. Pooling of effect estimates was prespecified to require at least three comparable studies per domain. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or AXIS.Results
Sixteen studies (19,529 participants; 1604 amputation events) provided usable effect estimates; 12 reported adjusted estimates from multivariable models. No domain contained three or more comparable estimates, so quantitative synthesis was not undertaken. Osteomyelitis was independently associated with amputation in both studies assessing it (aOR 5.60, 95% CI 2.93-10.78; aOR 11.8, 95% CI 5.1-27.5). Peripheral arterial disease was associated with LLA in two of three studies using objective vascular assessment (aOR 2.80, 95% CI 1.52-5.11; aOR 3.23 per grade, 95% CI 2.68-3.89). Prior amputation was associated with LLA in two DFU cohorts reporting concordant estimates (aOR 2.86 and 3.08). El resultado neutro plantea la cuestión de si el riesgo cardiovascular asociado a la elevación de la Lp(a) en el cuidado rutinario es suficientemente grande para producir beneficios clínicos detectables en ensayos clínicos en curso.

authors: Kumar-M P, Venkatakrishnan A, Montorzi M, Gibson CM, Soundararajan V.
abstract_en:
Importance: In the Lp(a)HORIZON trial, pelacarsen lowered lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] by 78% at 12 months without reducing major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). The neutral result raises the question of whether the cardiovascular risk associated with elevated Lp(a) in routine-care is sufficiently large to yield detectable clinical benefit in ongoing clinical trials. Objective:
 To quantify the association of Lp(a) with recurrent MACE and aortic valve outcomes in routine care, and to explore the implications of these associations for treatment-benefit scenarios in completed and ongoing Lp(a)-lowering trials. Design, Setting, and Participants: The study used a federated analysis of deidentified electronic health records across participating US academic medical centers. The primary retrospective cohort study analyzed adults aged 18 to 80 years with at least one Lp(a) measurement in routine care and documentation of a prior myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or symptomatic peripheral artery disease as of January 1, 2017 or later. Patients were followed for up to 5 years after meeting all inclusion criteria. Exposure: Baseline Lp(a), categorized as high (at least 150 nmol/L or 70 mg/dL) or low (less than 75 nmol/L or 30 mg/dL), and assessed continuously, including analyses stratified by baseline low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level. Main Outcomes and Measures: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization, and aortic stenosis or valve replacement, with hazard ratios (HRs) derived from adjusted Cox models. Results:
 Among 13,894 eligible patients, 13,865 contributed follow-up to outcome analyses. MACE occurred in 412 of 3,138 patients with high and 972 of 8,200 with low Lp(a) (5-year cumulative incidence, 20.1% vs 18.3%). The adjusted HR was 1.11 (95% CI, 0.98–1.25) after adjustment for age, sex, race, ethnicity, calendar year of entry, prior care, diagnosis frequency, and type and timing of the qualifying event. There was no consistent evidence of effect modification by LDL-C. In contrast, high Lp(a) was associated with aortic stenosis or valve replacement (HR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.11–2.36). Under the assumption that pharmacological Lp(a) lowering modifies the risk represented by the observational association, a model-based analysis yielded an illustrative HR of 0.95 (95% CI, 0.89–1.02) for the magnitude of Lp(a) reduction achieved in Lp(a)HORIZON. This estimate was compatible with the reported trial HR of 1.02 and represented a smaller benefit than the trial was powered to detect. Using trial-aligned routine-care cohorts, we then projected the treatment effects for ongoing phase 3 trials of olpasiran and lepodisiran, two Lp(a) lowering agents, based on the approximately 95% reduction in Lp(a) reported in their corresponding phase 2 trials. Under three different assumptions about the timing of clinical benefit, the modeled treatment HRs ranged from 0.94 to 0.98 for OCEAN(a)-Outcomes and 0.89 to 0.97 for ACCLAIM-Lp(a). Conclusions and Relevance: In this multicenter routine-care cohort, elevated Lp(a) showed a modest and statistically insignificant association with recurrent MACE, in contrast to a stronger association with aortic stenosis or valve replacement. Modeled projections based on the observed associations suggested that ongoing trials may not be powered to detect the estimated cardiovascular benefits of Lp(a) reduction. However, these projections do not establish the treatment effects of olpasiran or lepodisiran. The findings highlight the importance of trial population, treatment duration, and clinical endpoint selection, while supporting prospective evaluation of Lp(a)-lowering therapies for aortic valve disease.

Importancia: en el ensayo Lp(a)HORIZON, pelacarsen redujo la lipoproteína(a) [Lp(a)] en un 78% a los 12 meses sin reducir los eventos cardiovasculares adversos mayores (MACE). El resultado neutro plantea la cuestión de si el riesgo cardiovascular asociado a la elevación de la Lp(a) en el cuidado rutinario es suficientemente grande para producir beneficios clínicos detectables en ensayos clínicos en curso. Objetivo: cuantificar la asociación de la Lp(a) con los resultados recurrentes de la MACE y de la válvula aórtica en el cuidado rutinario, y explorar las implicaciones de estas asociaciones para los escenarios de tratamiento-beneficio en los ensayos Lp(a) en curso. Diseño, Ajuste y Participantes: El estudio utilizó un análisis federado de los registros de salud electrónicos desidentificados en los centros médicos académicos estadounidenses participantes. El estudio de cohorte retrospectivo primario analizó adultos de 18 a 80 años con al menos una Lp(a) medida en el cuidado rutinario y documentación de un infarto de miocardio previo, ictus isquémico o enfermedad arterial periférica sintomática a partir del 1 de enero de 2017 o más tarde. Exposición: Lp(a) basal, categorizada como alta (al menos 150 nmol/L o 70 mg/dL) o baja (menos de 75 nmol/L o 30 mg/dL), y evaluada continuamente, incluyendo análisis estratificados por el nivel basal de colesterol lipoproteico de baja densidad (LDL-C). Principales Resultados y Medidas: Eventos cardiovasculares adversos mayores (MACE), definidos como muerte cardiovascular, infarto de miocardio, ictus isquémico o revascularización coronaria urgente, y estenosis aórtica o reemplazo valvular, con índices de riesgo (HR) derivados de modelos ajustados de Cox. Resultados: Entre 13.894 pacientes elegibles, 13.865 contribuyeron al seguimiento de los análisis de resultados. El MACE se presentó en 412 de 3.138 pacientes con alto y 972 de 8.200 con bajo Lp(a) (incidencia acumulada a 5 años, 20,1% frente a 18,3%). La FC ajustada fue de 1,11 (IC 95%, 0,98–1,25) después de ajuste por edad, sexo, raza, etnia, año calendario de entrada, atención previa, frecuencia diagnóstica y tipo y momento del evento calificado. No hubo evidencia consistente de modificación del efecto por LDL-C. En contraste, la Lp(a) alta se asoció con estenosis aórtica o reemplazo valvular (HR, 1,62; IC 95%, 1,11–2,36). Bajo el supuesto de que la reducción farmacológica de Lp(a) modifica el riesgo representado por la asociación observacional, un análisis basado en modelos arrojó una FC ilustrativa de 0,95 (IC 95%, 0,89–1,02) para la magnitud de la reducción de Lp(a) alcanzada en Lp(a)HORIZON. Esta estimación fue compatible con la FC del ensayo notificado de 1,02 y representó un beneficio menor que el que se pudo detectar en el ensayo. Utilizando cohortes de cuidado rutinarias alineadas con el ensayo, se proyectaron los efectos del tratamiento para los ensayos en fase 3 en curso de olpasan y lepodisiran, dos agentes reductores de Lp(a) basados en la reducción de aproximadamente 95% en Lp(a) reportados en sus ensayos correspondientes de fase 2. Bajo tres supuestos diferentes sobre el tiempo de beneficio clínico, las FCs de tratamiento modeladas variaron de 0,94 a 0,98 para OCEAN(a)-Resultados y 0,89 a 0,97 para ACCLAM-Lp(a). Conclusiones y relevancia: En esta cohorte multicéntrico de cuidados rutinarios, la Lp(a) elevada mostró una asociación modesta y estadísticamente insignificante con MACE recurrente, en contraste con una asociación más fuerte con estenosis aórtica o reemplazo valvular. Proyecciones modeladas basadas en las asociaciones observadas sugieren que los ensayos en curso no pueden ser impulsados para detectar los beneficios cardiovasculares estimados de la reducción de Lp(a). Sin embargo, estas proyecciones no establecen los efectos del tratamiento de olpasirán o lepodisirán. Los hallazgos resaltan la importancia de la población del ensayo, la duración del tratamiento y la selección de los criterios de valoración clínicos, al tiempo que apoyan la evaluación prospectiva de las terapias de reducción de Lp(a) para la enfermedad valvular aórtica.

abstract_en: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has been linked to cardiovascular disease through inflammation-related pathways, but its association with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains uncertain. The purpose of this study was to systematically review and meta-analyze evidence on the association between CH mutations and AF, with planned analyses by hematologic cancer status, variant allele frequency (VAF), mutations, and sex. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 6, 2026, for studies reporting adjusted quantitative associations between CH and incident AF. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Study quality was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies-of Exposures tool. Five studies comprising 7 cohorts and 299,215 participants were included. In populations without cancer, CH defined by VAF ≥2% was not significantly associated with AF (HR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.97-1.07; I2 = 0%). Large CH clones (VAF ≥10%) were associated with a modestly higher AF risk (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.01-1.22; I2 = 0%). Mutation-specific analyses did not show statistically significant associations for DNMT3A, TET2, or ASXL1 individually, and no sex-based effect modification was observed. In hematologic cancer populations, CH mutations were significantly associated with higher AF risk (HR: 3.22; 95% CI: 1.02-10.13; I2 = 0%). Sensitivity analyses and wide prediction intervals warrant cautious interpretation, particularly for the VAF ≥10% and hematologic cancer analyses. The association between CH and AF may vary by clonal burden and hematologic cancer status. However, evidence remains limited and observational. Larger studies with standardized CH and AF definitions are needed to clarify clinical relevance.

Se realizaron meta-análisis de efectos aleatorios. La calidad del estudio se evaluó utilizando la herramienta Riesgo de Bias en Estudios no aleatorizados de Exposición. abstract_en: Cardiac surgery is associated with postoperative functional impairment that affects quality of life. Prehabilitation programmes may improve functional recovery in patients undergoing cardiac surgery who are at risk of postoperative complications. This systematic review aimed to present current evidence on the effectiveness of prehabilitation programmes in patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery. PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect were searched for relevant studies according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement and the Cochrane Collaboration Handbook. Eligible studies included adults undergoing cardiac surgery who participated in a prehabilitation programme. Only randomised controlled trials or clinical trials published in English were included. Outcomes of interest were respiratory function, exercise capacity and length of stay. Methodological quality was assessed using the PEDro (Physiotherapy Evidence Database) scale. The study was registered with the Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/NV3GF). The search identified 658 studies, of which 19 met the inclusion criteria. Most studies used inspiratory muscle training as the preoperative intervention. Prehabilitation significantly increased maximal inspiratory pressure in six studies and the 6-minute walk test in five of seven studies, while reducing mechanical ventilation duration in six studies, intensive care unit length of stay in four of seven studies and postoperative pulmonary complications. Methodological quality was moderate, with a median score of 5 (range, 2-8). Prehabilitation exercise-based programmes improve inspiratory muscle strength and functional capacity while reducing postoperative pulmonary complications, mechanical ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay.

abstract_en:
Aims
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are an integral part of heart failure (HF) therapy. The purpose of this study was to elucidate the effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on renal function, in HF patients, over longer-term follow-up. This could be compared to existing data in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus T2DM.Methods
A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in patients with HF treated with SGLT2 inhibitor (PROSPERO ID: CRD42024562311). Searches were performed across five databases from inception to 31 October 2024 identifying randomised controlled trials. Included studies were appraised using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Two primary outcomes were investigated, composite renal event and AKI (acute kidney injury). Relative risk (RR) was pooled with 95% CI using the statistical software 'R'.Results
Thirteen trials involving 90,413 participants were included. Median follow-up was 2.3 years, and data of 32,957 patients with HF was extracted. In patients with HF, SGLT2 inhibition reduced renal specific composite outcomes by 28% (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.57-0.91). Additionally, AKI was reduced in HF patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors (RR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65-0.86). Subgroup analysis showed no differences in patients with and without HF, or when stratified by baseline renal function.Conclusion
These results encourage use of SGLT2 inhibitors to retard progression of kidney disease and AKI. This benefit was seen in all trials, irrespective of concurrent comorbidities. Despite the acute dip in eGFR, SGLT2 inhibitors should be continued to maximise benefit, even in patients with HF.

abstract_en: Abstract  Background  Four-point scleral fixation is increasingly used for secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in eyes without adequate capsular support, yet pooled estimates of its visual benefit and complication profile are lacking. We aimed to quantify visual outcomes and postoperative complications after four-point scleral IOL fixation. Methods  This systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 and registered retrospectively in OSF Registries (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/DTY7X). The final searches of PubMed, Embase, Europe PMC and the Cochrane Library (CENTRAL) were completed on 5 November 2026. Studies of ≥ 4 eyes undergoing sutured or flanged four-point scleral fixation of a posterior chamber IOL were included. Within-study changes in logMAR visual acuity and intraocular pressure (IOP) were pooled with random-effects models (REML with Hartung-Knapp adjustment), and complication incidences with random-intercept logistic generalized linear mixed models. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and an adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Results  Sixty-seven studies (approximately 3,250 eyes; two randomized) were included. Best-corrected visual acuity improved by 0.57 logMAR (95% CI 0.44–0.70; 37 studies, 1,552 eyes; I² = 97%) and uncorrected distance visual acuity by 0.83 logMAR (95% CI 0.53–1.14; 7 studies, 211 eyes). Results were robust in sensitivity analyses and did not differ by suture material or technique (p = 0.56). Mean IOP fell slightly (0.97 mmHg, 95% CI 0.02–1.93; 17 studies). The most frequent complications were ocular hypertension (15.9%, 95% CI 12.4–20.3), cystoid macular oedema (10.1%, 7.2–14.0), corneal oedema (9.9%, 5.3–17.7) and hypotony (7.5%, 5.1–10.9). Other pooled incidences were glaucoma (4.2%), vitreous haemorrhage (4.3%), IOL tilt/decentration (2.4%), retinal detachment (1.5%), IOL dislocation (1.3%), endophthalmitis (0.7%) and suture-related complications (0.8%). Certainty of evidence was very low across all assessed outcomes. Conclusions  Four-point scleral fixation of posterior chamber IOLs was associated with improved visual acuity and a low incidence of serious postoperative complications, including retinal detachment, IOL dislocation and endophthalmitis. Ocular hypertension and cystoid macular oedema were among the most frequently reported complications, highlighting the importance of postoperative monitoring. However, the very low certainty of the available evidence limits the strength of these conclusions. Further prospective comparative studies with standardized outcome definitions and long-term follow-up are warranted to better define the efficacy and safety of four-point fixation relative to alternative IOL fixation techniques.

abstract_en:
Topic
Whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use is associated with a lower risk of incident glaucoma or ocular hypertension (OHT) in adults, and whether the association differs by diabetes status or comparator.Clinical relevance
Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, and every licensed treatment targets lowering intraocular pressure (IOP); none protects retinal ganglion cells directly. GLP-1RAs are widely prescribed and have been proposed to be neuroprotective, so whether this class of medication alters glaucoma risk matters at prescribing and to the search for pressure-independent treatment. Four earlier meta-analyses found no significant association but pooled non-equivalent comparators.Methods
Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies, following PRISMA 2020 and registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251082642). PubMed was searched on 15 April 2026 and updated to 30 August 2026, with CENTRAL, Europe PMC, the first 100 Google Scholar results and bidirectional citation tracking as supplementary sources. Eligible studies were retrospective cohort or nested case-control studies of GLP-1RA exposure with incident glaucoma, OHT or IOP change as the outcome and with adjustment for confounding. Two reviewers screened, extracted and applied ROBINS-I. Estimates were pooled by DerSimonian-Laird random effects, with a Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) interval, a 95% prediction interval and GRADE.Results
Ten studies were included from 406 screened records. Six cohorts covering 225,814 matched or analysed patients were pooled. GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower incidence of recorded glaucoma or OHT (pooled hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.80; HKSJ CI 0.56 to 0.85), but heterogeneity was 58.5%, the 95% prediction interval (0.44 to 1.08) included no effect, and certainty was low. The association held after all TriNetX studies were removed (0.78, 0.71 to 0.85) and after restriction to open-angle outcomes (0.66, 0.53 to 0.82). Diabetes status, comparator type and data platform could not be separated.Conclusion
Low-certainty observational evidence suggests GLP-1RA use is not associated with a higher risk of glaucoma or OHT and may be associated with a lower one. Confounding by indication, coded outcome ascertainment and a prediction interval that includes no effect mean protection has not been shown. The findings support reassurance and the randomized trial under way.

abstract_en: BackgroundAdjusting pump speed in patients with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) during exercise may improve hemodynamics and enhance functional capacity in advanced heart failure, but its clinical benefit over fixed-speed operation remains uncertain. We evaluated whether dynamic, exercise-driven LVAD speed modulation improves physical performance compared to fixed-speed settings.Methods and resultsPubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing dynamic adjustment versus fixed pump speed control during exercise in patients with LVADs. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using mean differences (MD), and binary outcomes using risk ratios (RR), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical analysis was performed using R (version 4.3.1). Eight studies were included, with study sample sizes totaling 124 participants; seven used crossover designs and one used a non-randomized repeated-measures design. abstract_en: Vernakalant is an atrial-selective antiarrhythmic drug for the rapid conversion of recent-onset atrial fibrillation, but its effectiveness relative to alternative drugs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis included studies comparing intravenous vernakalant with another antiarrhythmic drug in adults with recent-onset atrial fibrillation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through March 2026. The primary outcome was conversion to sinus rhythm; secondary outcomes were time to conversion, electrical cardioversion, and adverse events. Random-effects models, trial sequential analysis, and GRADE were used. Nine studies (3 randomized, 1 quasi-randomized, and 5 observational; 1788 patients or episodes) compared vernakalant with amiodarone, ibutilide, flecainide, procainamide, or propafenone. Conversion occurred in 69.0% of patients receiving vernakalant and 53.0% of those receiving a comparator (odds ratio [OR], 2.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.51-4.21; I2 = 72%). Heterogeneity was explained by the amiodarone comparisons (OR, 18.14; interaction P < 0.001); against the other comparators, the OR was 1.77 (95% CI, 1.41-2.22; I2 = 0%). Vernakalant shortened time to conversion among responders (mean difference, -19.3 minutes; 95% CI, -24.2 to -14.4) and reduced electrical cardioversion (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.34-0.73), without a significant difference in adverse events (OR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.57-1.08). The cumulative Z-curve crossed the trial sequential monitoring boundary, but the certainty of evidence was low for all outcomes.

abstract_en:
Background
Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for several cardiovascular diseases, leading to the need for investigations of user-friendly and less costly nonpharmacological interventions, including passive heat therapies. This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential.Methods
We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. The review protocol was not preregistered.Results
Acute blood-pressure reductions and changes in vascular or autonomic markers were reported in some populations, but sustained comparative effects in hypertension remain uncertain. In hypertensive participants, both hot and thermoneutral immersion were associated with reductions in 24-h blood pressure (BP), limiting heat-specific attribution. A single pooled effect estimate and corresponding 95% confidence interval were not calculated. The benefits were linked to lower sympathetic activity, more nitric oxide availability, lower endothelin-1 levels, and less oxidative stress. Outcome-specific GRADE certainty was very low for SBP and DBP and the assessed mechanistic domains.Conclusion
Passive heat exposure can produce short-term reductions in BP and changes in vascular function, but sustained antihypertensive efficacy, particularly when evaluated with 24-h ambulatory BP in patients with established hypertension, remains uncertain. Mechanistic findings from heart-failure and peripheral artery disease (PAD) cohorts are indirect evidence for uncomplicated hypertension. Passive heat should not replace established antihypertensive treatment. Safety evidence is limited to selected, often supervised populations, and larger trials with ambulatory BP and systematic adverse-event assessment are needed.

abstract_en: Acute pain in the postoperative period and pre-existing cognitive impairment (CI) are both independently associated with increased postoperative adverse outcomes. Pre-existing cognitive impairment may interfere with the reporting, recognition, and treatment of pain in this population. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the impact of pre-existing cognitive impairment on pain and analgesic consumption after surgery in adults. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews were searched for randomized controlled trials and cohort studies for adults undergoing non-cardiac, emergency, or elective surgery until April 9, 2026. Surgical patients with pre-existing cognitive impairment were compared to cognitively intact peers. The primary outcomes assessed were subjective ratings of pain and analgesic consumption postoperatively. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence was rated by GRADE. Meta-analysis used standard mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals. Thirteen studies (37,918 patients) were included. Approximately one third (33%; 95% CI 0.25-0.41) of adult surgical patients screened positive for preoperative cognitive impairment. Subjective pain scores did not differ significantly between patients with and without cognitive impairment (Hedge's g: 0.11 (SD -0.15-0.36, I2 85.3%, T2 0.073). Patients with cognitive impairment had significantly less analgesic consumption than their cognitively intact counterparts (Cohen's d: 0.53 (0.29-0.76, I2 67.4%, T2 0.028). Despite comparable pain scores, those with cognitive impairment received significantly less postoperative analgesia, raising concern for systematic under-recognition and undertreatment of pain. Increased awareness of this discrepancy and the use of standardized analgesia protocols may improve postoperative outcomes. International Registry of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO:1117357).

El dolor agudo en el postoperatorio y el deterioro cognitivo preexistente (IC) se asocian de forma independiente con el aumento de los resultados adversos postoperatorios, pudiendo interferir con el reporte, reconocimiento y tratamiento del dolor en esta población, y esta revisión sistemática y metaanálisis evaluó el impacto del deterioro cognitivo preexistente en el dolor y el consumo analgésico después de la cirugía en adultos. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central y Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews fueron buscados para ensayos aleatorizados controlados y estudios de cohortes en adultos sometidos a cirugía no cardiaca, de emergencia o electiva hasta el 9 de abril de 2026. Los pacientes quirúrgicos con deterioro cognitivo preexistente fueron comparados con los cognoscitivamente intactos, los principales resultados evaluados fueron las calificaciones subjetivas del dolor y el consumo analgésico postoperatorio, el riesgo de sesgo fue evaluado con ROBINS-I y la certeza de la evidencia fue calificada con GRADE. El metaanálisis utilizó diferencias medias estándar (DME) con intervalos de confianza del 95%. Se incluyeron 13 estudios (37.918 pacientes). Aproximadamente un tercio (33%; IC 95% 0,25-0.41) de pacientes quirúrgicos adultos evaluados positivos por deterioro cognitivo preoperatorio. Los puntajes de dolor subjetivo no difirieron significativamente entre los pacientes con y sin deterioro cognitivo (G de Hedge: 0,11 (SD -0.15-0.36, I2 85,3%, T2 0.073).Los pacientes con deterioro cognitivo tuvieron un consumo de analgésicos significativamente menor que sus contrapartes cognitivamente intactas (D de Cohen: 0,53 (0,29-0,76, I2 67,4%, T2 0.028).A pesar de los puntajes de dolor comparables, los pacientes con deterioro cognitivo recibieron una analgesia postoperatoria significativamente menor, lo que generó preocupación por el subreconocimiento sistemático y el subtratamiento del dolor. Registro Internacional de Exámenes Sistemáticos (PROSPERO:1117357).

abstract_en:
Aim
To evaluate the use of intra-arrest blood pressure monitoring and association between blood pressure thresholds and outcomes in infants and children.Methods
A systematic review was performed, registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024590080). We executed the search strategy on MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials all years until April 1, 2026. We used GRADE and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale to assess the evidence found. Critically important outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge, and survival with favourable neurological outcome, as defined in the Paediatric Core Outcome Set for Cardiac Arrest.Results
Six studies were included in the final analysis. Two studies (577 events) were pooled. A diastolic blood pressure (DBP) of ≥25 mmHg for infants Conclusion
In infants and children with invasive arterial monitoring in place during IHCA, a DBP of ≥25 mmHg (infants) or ≥30 mmHg (children) during the first 10 min of CPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcome. The evidence is observational and of very low certainty, and does not establish that titrating resuscitation to these thresholds improves outcomes.The protocol for this systematic review was registered as PROSPERO ID CRD42024590080.

abstract_en: Background/Objectives: Pediatric guidelines retain induced hypothermia as an option, but its optimal duration is uncertain. We compared survival and favorable neurologic outcomes across duration-specific strategies. Methods: Five databases and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through 20 August 2026. A random-effects network meta-analysis compared 24, 48, and 72 h hypothermia (HT) with heterogeneous Control strategies. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions tool; certainty was assessed using Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA). Results: Survival included five studies (three randomized, two observational; 785 participants), and neurologic outcomes included four (three randomized, one observational; 615 participants). HT-72 h was associated with higher survival than Control (risk ratio [RR], 2.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.24-3.25); 72% of this estimate derived from one observational study measuring 1-month survival, versus 12 months in the randomized 48 h trials. The estimate versus HT-48 h (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.05-2.97) was entirely indirect and depended on merging different Control strategies. The neurologic estimate versus Control (RR, 10.92; 95% CI, 1.32-90.40) depended on a single observational study at serious risk of bias and was extremely imprecise. Superiority over shorter durations was not robust. Certainty for HT-72 h versus Control was very low for both outcomes. Conclusions: Evidence remains compatible with equipoise and does not establish an optimal duration. Funding: No external funding. Registration: Open Science Framework, 10.17605/OSF.IO/9MNDB (retrospective).

Antecedentes/Objetivos: Las guías pediátricas retienen la hipotermia inducida como opción, pero su duración óptima es incierta. Se comparó la supervivencia y los resultados neurológicos favorables en estrategias específicas de duración. Métodos: Se buscaron cinco bases de datos y ClinicalTrials.gov hasta el 20 de agosto de 2026. Se comparó un metaanálisis de la red de efectos aleatorios con la hipotermia (HT) de 24, 48 y 72 h con estrategias de control heterogéneas. Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo utilizando la herramienta Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 y la herramienta Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions; se evaluó la certeza mediante la confianza en la metaanálisis de red (CINeMA). Resultados: La supervivencia incluyó cinco estudios (tres aleatorizados, dos observacionales; 785 participantes) y los resultados neurológicos fueron cuatro (tres aleatorizados, uno observacional; 615 participantes). La HT-72 h se asoció con una supervivencia mayor que la de Control (cociente de riesgo [RR], 2,01; intervalo de confianza del 95% [IC], 1,24-3,25); el 72% de esta estimación derivada de un estudio observacional que midió la supervivencia de 1 mes, frente a 12 meses en los ensayos aleatorizados de 48 h. La estimación versus HT-48 h (RR, 1,77; IC del 95%, 1,05-2,97) fue totalmente indirecta y dependió de la fusión de diferentes estrategias de control. La estimación neurológica versus Control (RR, 10.92; IC 95%, 1.32-90.40) dependía de un único estudio observacional con riesgo grave de sesgo y era extremadamente imprecisa. La superioridad en duraciones más cortas no era robusta. La certeza para HT-72 h versus Control era muy baja para ambos resultados. Conclusiones: La evidencia sigue siendo compatible con la equipaise y no establece una duración óptima. Financiación: No hay financiación externa. Registro: Open Science Framework, 10.17605/OSF.IO/9MNDB (retrospectiva).

abstract_en:
Introduction
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly entering obstetrics and prenatal medicine, particularly in prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal magnetic resonance imaging, genomic screening, risk prediction and clinical decision support. The aim of this review was to summarize current evidence, recent developments and implementation requirements for AI-based applications in prenatal care.Materials and methods
A structured narrative review was performed with emphasis on peer-reviewed and clinically relevant literature published from 2021 to 2026, supplemented by landmark methodological, regulatory and reporting guidance. Priority was given to systematic reviews, diagnostic accuracy studies, external validation studies, prospective evaluations, randomized educational or clinical studies, regulatory documents and reporting standards relevant to AI in medicine.Results
The strongest current evidence supports AI-assisted standard-plane recognition, image-quality assessment and fetal biometry, followed by emerging applications in fetal cardiac screening, blind-sweep ultrasound, fetal MRI segmentation, placental phenotyping, prediction of fetal growth restriction, preterm birth and preeclampsia, and machine learning-enhanced cfDNA analysis. Generative and multimodal AI systems may support report drafting, guideline retrieval and education, but remain insufficiently validated for autonomous clinical decision-making.Discussion
AI has the potential to improve access, standardization, efficiency and quality assurance in prenatal medicine. However, most applications remain limited by retrospective design, enriched datasets, insufficient external validation, unclear calibration, limited fairness analyses and incomplete workflow evaluation. Clinical adoption should therefore follow a human-in-the-loop model with prospective validation, transparent reporting, regulatory oversight, bias monitoring and post-market surveillance. AI should augment rather than replace specialist expertise in obstetrics and fetal medicine.

Introducción La inteligencia artificial (IA) entra cada vez más en la obstetricia y la medicina prenatal, particularmente en la ecografía prenatal, la ecocardiografía fetal, la resonancia magnética fetal, el cribado genómico, la predicción de riesgos y el apoyo a la decisión clínica.El objetivo de esta revisión fue resumir la evidencia actual, los desarrollos recientes y los requisitos de implementación para las aplicaciones basadas en IA en la atención prenatal. Se dio prioridad a revisiones sistemáticas, estudios de precisión diagnóstica, estudios de validación externa, evaluaciones prospectivas, estudios educativos o clínicos aleatorizados, documentos regulatorios y estándares de reporte relevantes para la IA en medicina.Resultados La evidencia más fuerte actual apoya el reconocimiento estándar del plano asistido por IA, evaluación de calidad de imagen y biometría fetal, seguida de aplicaciones emergentes en el cribado cardíaco fetal, ultrasonido ciego, segmentación de la IRM fetal, fenotipado placentario, predicción de restricción del crecimiento fetal, nacimiento prematuro y preeclampsia, y análisis de cfDNA mejorado por aprendizaje automático. Los sistemas de IA genéricos y multimodales pueden apoyar la redacción de informes, la recuperación de directrices y la educación, pero siguen sin estar suficientemente validados para la adopción de decisiones clínicas autónomas.La IA de debate tiene el potencial de mejorar el acceso, la estandarización, la eficiencia y la garantía de calidad en medicina prenatal.Sin embargo, la mayoría de las aplicaciones siguen limitadas por el diseño retrospectivo, conjuntos de datos enriquecidos, validación externa insuficiente, calibración poco clara, análisis de equidad limitados y evaluación incompleta del flujo de trabajo. La IA debería aumentar en lugar de sustituir a los especialistas en obstetricia y medicina fetal.

abstract_en: Occlusive myocardial infarction (OMI) is a specific, high-risk subgroup of non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. To estimate the impact of this clinical entity, this post-hoc analysis of the SLIM trial uses decreased TIMI flow (0 or 1) and patent flow (TIMI 2-3 flow) as surrogates to characterize these patient groups and their outcomes in a cohort with NSTEMI and multivessel coronary artery disease. The SLIM trial randomized NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease to complete or culprit-only revascularization; we included 474 patients with available angiographic data in the current analysis. One-year Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: all-cause death, non-fatal MI, any revascularization, and stroke) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and the association between study groups and outcomes was evaluated in crude and adjusted Cox proportional-hazards models. TIMI 0-1 patients were younger (62 vs. 67 years, p<0.001), predominantly male (84.9% vs. 69.3%, p<0.001), with higher baseline biomarker levels. Routine interpretation of admission ECGs failed to differentiate occlusion status (reported ST-deviation 32.1% vs. 33.2%, p = 0.835). In the TIMI 0-1 flow group, the circumflex artery was the culprit more often (45.3% vs. 27.7%, p < 0.001). Although unadjusted MACE at 1-year follow-up was comparable (p=0.061), adjusted models showed that decreased flow was associated with MACE at one year (MACE: aHR 2.09, p=0.026). This post-hoc analysis of the SLIM trial shows that TIMI 0-1 flow during the index procedure is an indicator for a high-risk subgroup of NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease who face a higher risk of MACE at one year.

Para estimar el impacto de esta entidad clínica, este análisis post-hoc del ensayo SLIM utiliza el flujo TIMI disminuido (0 ó 1) y el flujo patente (flujo TIMI 2-3) como sustitutos para caracterizar a estos grupos de pacientes y sus resultados en una cohorte con IAMEST y enfermedad de las arterias coronarias multivaso. El ensayo SLIM al azar pacientes con IAMEST con enfermedad multivaso para completar o solo la revascularización culpable; se incluyeron 474 pacientes con datos angiográficos disponibles en el análisis actual. Se evaluaron los eventos cardiovasculares adversos mayores de un año (MACE: muerte por todas las causas, IAM no mortal, revascularización e ictus) utilizando el análisis de supervivencia de Kaplan-Meier, y se evaluó la asociación entre los grupos de estudio y los resultados en modelos de riesgo proporcional de Cox crudos y ajustados. Los pacientes con IAMT 0-1 fueron más jóvenes (62 vs. 67 años, p<0,001), predominantemente varones (84,9% vs. 69,3%, p<0,001), con niveles de biomarcador basal más altos. La interpretación rutinaria de los ECG de admisión no logró diferenciar el estado de oclusión (desviación del ST reportada 32,1% vs. 33,2%, p = 0,835); en el grupo de flujo TIMI 0-1, la arteria circunfleja fue la causa más frecuente (45,3% vs. 27,7%, p < 0,001). Aunque el MACE no ajustado a 1 año de seguimiento fue comparable (p=0,061), los modelos ajustados mostraron que la disminución del flujo se asoció con MACE a un año (MACE: aHR 2,09, p=0,026). Este análisis post-hoc del ensayo SLIM muestra que el flujo TIMI 0-1 durante el procedimiento del índice es un indicador para un subgrupo de alto riesgo de pacientes con EIMEST con enfermedad multivaso que enfrentan un mayor riesgo de EAM a un año.
